description: Controlled 2x2 (backend x tuning-effort) on the current vintage to explain the _267 H=200 shortfall (agent-tuned XGBoost < sweep CatBoost). All arms: date-aligned, test window 2023-07-27..2024-10-03, --snapshot-end 2026-06-20.
metric: R-Precision@K (per-day fixed K, macro over days R_q>0, min(K,R_q) denominator)

design.catboost_sweep: *_aligned_resnap (default HP, <=3-iter FS+HP) = _267 bar re-run on current vintage

findings.vintage: REJECTED — current-vintage CatBoost sweep ~= stale sweep (sp500/40 identical; others within +-0.05).
findings.backend: DOMINANT — CatBoost has lowest eval->test decay (+0.065..+0.190 @1) and best test top-1/@3 in all 3 cells; no XGBoost variant beats CatBoost-sweep at @1/@3. (_225 pattern.)
findings.eval_overfit: SECONDARY + cell-dependent — agent eval-R-p@1 loop RESCUED a pathological XGBoost-default on sp500 (test @1 0.24/0.30 -> 0.62/0.70) but OVER-FIT a good default on russell (default 0.633 -> tuned 0.447). eval R-p@1 weakly/negatively coupled to test R-p@1 at H=200.
findings.capacity: NOT limiting — tiny agent models (depth 2-4) match CatBoost on sp500; failure is selection, not capacity.

recommendation: For H=200 cells default to the CatBoost sweep (robust, strong, cheap). Do not deploy agent-tuned XGBoost over it. If XGBoost is required, validate the agent pick vs XGBoost-default AND CatBoost-sweep. Loop fix: eval R-p@1 is a poor single-window target at H=200 (use longer/multi-window eval or a decay-penalized objective). Follow-up: CatBoost agent-tune (V1.5_TBD).
followup: docs/gbdt/V1.5_TBD.md: CatBoost agent-tune vs CatBoost sweep on H=200.
